issue.title: Let agents hand off a foreground sase tool run check that outlived its expected duration

task_type_fields.proposal:
Let an agent hand off a long `sase tool run check` that is already running in the foreground, without rerunning it.

Evidence (proposed by phase sase-1nf.14.1.2, note #1, 2026-10-27): ToolRun
`82acd74f80bfc0ab91b7fc4d8b746743` (`just check`) ran inside a SASE agent with
`SASE_AGENT_NAME`/`SASE_BEAD_ID` set. `sase tool show` records `LAUNCH foreground`,
`CONTEXT provider codex · ceiling — · soft —`, and a 100m 39s duration (it succeeded).
Because the provider exported no `SASE_PROVIDER_SYNC_CEILING_SECONDS`, inline-then-escalate
(sase-1cx / sase-17g) never detached the run. Once it was clearly long (a stale context
baseline 4,719 commits behind selected 933 files), `sase monitor start -J <run>` refused it:
only starter-scoped detached runs can be joined. The only way to hand it off was to cancel
and restart it, which the verification guidance forbids, so the agent's turn stayed blocked
for over 30 minutes.

Possible remediations, for the worker to choose: (a) give agent `sase tool run` a default
sync budget even when the provider has no ceiling, so long checks always escalate into a
joinable detached run; or (b) let `sase monitor start -J` safely adopt a foreground run owned
by the calling agent, with an ownership handoff that survives the turn ending.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope:
Epic sase-1nf.14.1 reduces TUI GC producers and measures acceptance. This is a ToolRun
routing/monitor-join design question in the sase tool control plane that the epic's coder
only ran into while verifying. Changing it needs its own decision about agent sync budgets
or ownership transfer (see decisions record-before-admit / explicit-handoff-fails-closed).

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1nf.14.1.2 could not move a 100-minute inline check to a monitor: no provider ceiling meant no escalation, and monitor -J refuses non-detached runs.

payload.description: sibling monitor -J join limitation; -f prepared completion with join
inline-then-escalate design that only escalates when a provider ceiling exists
Long foreground checks that cannot be handed off make a starved token wait block the agent turn

evidence.note: Independent completed reproduction in sase-1ou.6.land--3: inline check 327c36b33b7f93515c353a754a7ff9c5 broadened on core-identity-changed and occupied this provider turn for 13,598,804 ms (226m39s), with one pytest worker. No sync ceiling/escalation occurred; joining a foreground run is unsupported. The command was kept running to completion, never canceled or rerun. Final result: 59,102 passed, 17 skipped, 10 pre-existing failures; no_new_failures verdict, exit 1. This is concrete operational impact of the same requested foreground-to-monitor continuation capability.
